USAGE:
    fur database restore [database] [file] [OPTIONS]

ARGUMENTS:
    [database]    Name of the database to restore. Not required when using --all
    [file]        Path to the dump file to restore. If not provided, looks for  
                  <database>.dump in the current directory                      

OPTIONS:
    -h, --help                  Prints help information                         
    -H, --host                  Database host address                           
    -p, --port                  Database port                                   
    -U, --username              Database username                               
    -W, --password              Database password. If not provided, will be     
                                resolved from user config or prompted           
                                interactively                                   
        --ssl-mode              SSL mode for the database connection (Disable,  
                                Prefer, Require, VerifyCA, VerifyFull)          
        --timeout               Timeout in seconds for the restore operation    
        --command-timeout       Command timeout in seconds for the restore      
                                operation                                       
    -a, --all                   Restore all databases from dump files in the    
                                specified directory                             
    -d, --directory             Directory containing .dump files (for --all). If
                                not provided, uses current directory            
    -v, --verbose               Enable verbose output from pg_restore           
        --no-clean              Do not drop database objects before creating    
                                them. By default, --clean is used               
        --no-owner              Skip restoration of object ownership            
        --no-acl                Skip restoration of access privileges           
        --single-transaction    Execute the restore as a single transaction     
    -j, --jobs                  Number of parallel jobs for restore             
                                (custom-format only)
